sections.text: He whose mind is entirely detached, who has conquered himself, whose desires have vanished, by his renunciation reaches that stage of perfect freedom where action completes itself and leaves no seed.
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे।
I will now state briefly how he, who has reached perfection, finds the Eternal Spirit, the state of Supreme Wisdom.
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च।
Guided always by pure reason, bravely restraining himself, renouncing the objects of sense and giving up attachment and hatred;

We had been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasi Yoga, Yoga of Liberation through renunciation, renunciation of actions. Up till now we have discussed the nature of actions, the nature of actors -- that is, you and I -- and the nature of knowledge. Knowledge that propels my desires, and my desires prompt me to act. And I go and act in this world outside.
So we have analyzed how we function in this world. We came to the conclusion that depending on the texture of my mind and intellect, whether it is Sattvik, Rajaseek or Tamasvik thats dependent on my tendencies. If my tendencies are Sattvik, I will have Sattvik desires and I will do Sattvik actions.
If they are Rajasik, the same applies, and Tamasic appropriately. So my tendencies are driving my actions. And from these actions come reactions from the world, and I react to those, and they become my further actions.
This cycle continues as long as I have the sense of doership and Bhokta Bhava, which is the sense of enjoyership. I am the doer and Im the enjoyer. And therefore we have analyzed in detail what is the nature of the action, what is the nature of the actor, and what is the nature of knowledge.
So the prescription we have seen in the last verse we had been discussing says Sahajam Karma Kaunteya, do the actions which come naturally to you? Because after analyzing all these actions we get confused. Maybe the only Sattvic actions should be done. I should give up all the Rajasic and Tamasic actions.
But thats not possible for any one of us, because what we dont have control over is our tendencies. The tendencies came from my past experiences. I do not have any control over my past.
I have control over my present, and I dont have any control over my future. But my present actions can determine what my future will be. I can control the present to shape my future.
So therefore Bhagavan says after knowing all this, that the actions and actors can be Satvika, Raja, Sikh and Tamastik and their consequences, the results of those actions. So what am I supposed to do, Bhagavan? Bhagavan said, sahajam Karma Kaunteya. You do the actions which come naturally to you at this time, because you have these accumulated vasanas and tendencies which you cannot get rid of overnight or just because you read Bhagavad Gita for half an hour in the morning.
So Bhagavan said, do the actions which come naturally to you -- Sahajam Karma Kaunteya -- not the ones which I find to be the best actions to perform in this field or environment, but that which comes natural to me due to the tendencies of my mind and my intellect. Sadosham Api Na Tyajet. Now, I come to the conclusion that my desire is to do designs for buildings.
But then the clients come to me. Their projects may have some defects. I had clients who had tobacco companies.
I have casinos as my client, and I even had a strip club as my client. In 2001, we were in our downtown Brook Binder building and there was a strip club on Brook Road. They called us up and said, Somebody recommended your name and we need your help doing some modifications to our club because there are some code violations. So my staff who fielded the phone came to me and said, Rajan, this is a problem. I dont think youre going to allow it. I said, Of course Im going to allow it.
The client is a form of God. Gandhiji said, Grahaka Iti Bhagavan -- the customer is Gods representative. I said, our job is to fix the code violations. Go and find out what the code violations are, figure out what needs to be done, give them the appropriate drawings, and make sure the code violations are mitigated.
What he does is between him and his Bhagavan. What I do is between I and my Bhagavan. My Bhagavan says, your job as an architect to make sure if a client comes to you to get his building more in line with the local codes, you need to help him.
Even actions with defects should not be given up. Because imagine if all architects say, Well, we are not helping any strip clubs anymore -- what happens? It will be a building full of fire violations, code violations, dangerous for the society. So Bhagawan said, even if your actions seem to have defects, because they come naturally to you, they should not be given up.
Sarva Arambahi Doshena Dhumena Agnihi Ava Vritaha -- all actions (arambha in this case means actions). What is considered arambha: Im doing it because I want to do it, to fulfill my desire. Any arambha will have its own defects.
Any medication will have its own side effect. Any action prompted by your desire will have its own side effects. So Bhagavan said thats given that the nature of any action.
Therefore even if you find that something you are doing out of your nature and find a fault in it, you should not give up. Because every action if you analyze will have its own defects. Dhumena agnihi ava vritaha -- just as every fire will have smoke.
Some fires may have more smoke, some may have very little. But there is smoke, because there is no combustion that we know of in our day-to-day life which is hundred percent combustion. Therefore there will be smoke.
But that does not mean that you give up lighting fire when you need it. Therefore you should continue to perform actions which comes naturally to you even though they may have defects. Now, if I work in this world in that manner, what should I expect? What happens is that when you are aligning your actions with your nature, the ego pressure will reduce.
All the problems we see in our life come from egocentric actions. But when I do something which comes naturally to me, there will not be any ego pressure. And therefore you will gradually become asaktabuddhehe -- your intellect will become unattached.
When you do something which comes naturally to you, there is very little ego involved in it. And therefore you dont get attached to that. Sarvatra -- your intellect becomes unattached in all actions that you perform which come naturally to you.
Because now your intellect is not attached, its not creating more vasanas. Where we create more vasanas is when we get polluted by the experience in the field. For example, I go to the mall and all I want to do is buy one thing.
But while Im there, I get affected by the environment. I went with a list of 10 items and I came back with 18 items. Thats how the environment affects us.
If Im consciously working in tune with my own nature, then I will be least affected by the environment. Therefore I will have the least creation of new vasanas, and the pressure of new vasanas will be at a minimum. So I will be Jitatma -- I will have control over myself.
Now anytime we say the self, we mean my mind, my intellect, and my senses. So Jitatma Vigataspruhaha -- one becomes without any desires. This may be very difficult for us to grasp.
But the more you function in line with your nature, the more you get success in that field. And you have less and less desire to do things which are not in line with your nature. So therefore you become Vigataspruhaha -- without any additional desires.
Im exhausting my past vasanas which created my tendencies, which put me into this field of activities. Im exhausting my past vasanas by doing so. And therefore Im getting least and least attached to my actions.
And when I exhaust those vasanas, Ill have less and less desires. Because Im only focused on the what I like. Niskarima siddhiyam paramam sanyasena adigachati.
What was my final goal is to renounce actions. But right now, because of my past vasanas and the vasana pressures and my tendencies, I cannot renounce them. So Bhagavan said, go ahead and act in this field which is in tune with your true nature.
By doing so you will get less and less the sense of doership and sense of enjoyership. And therefore you will not take credit or blame for those actions. You will say, This is what I do, this is what I wanted to do, and I did it.
What came out of it was not in my hand. More and more you give up that sense of doership. Actions become non-actions because youre not taking any credit for them. If you act on behalf of your company and things go completely wrong -- but you did it exactly as per the companys policies and what your job description calls for -- would you be totally worried about that? Thats the companys problem.
Why did they have this wrong policy? They asked me to do this. I, as a project manager or the VP, did it. Those happen to be the wrong policies.
As long as you thought that you took the decision and were guiding the companys policy, then you are in trouble. But you are working on behalf of the company. What you do is strictly the companys liability.
Even though Bhagavan has given us all these capabilities, we take the responsibility and therefore we suffer for it. So Bhagavan said, when you reach a point where your actions become natural, you are not taking the credit or blame for them. You offer everything to him who has given you this talent.
So Bhagavan said, as long as you recognize that most of your ability to function in this world has come in spite of you, that sense will give you Naishkarmya Siddhi -- you will reach a state of actionlessness. And if you think about it, thats what we were trying to do in the first place! I was working towards my retirement, right? All this 401k and all that Im putting together for my retirement -- an actionless state. Naishkarmya Siddhim Paramam -- he achieves the highest state of actionlessness.
And therefore, Sanyasena Adhigacchati. And therefore he renounces all the sense of doership and enjoyership and achieves the highest state of complete bliss. The next verse says Siddhim Prapto Yatha Brahma Tata Apnoti Nibodhame Samase Naivakante Nishtha Gnanasya Yapara.
We have come full circle. We have understood who we are, how we work in this world. And we also got the prescription of Bhagavan.
So now Bhagavan said, okay, now that he understood all of that. Now if you follow this advice, then what will happen? Siddhim Prapto yatha Brahma Tatha Apnoti Nibodhame ultimate goal was to reach the state of infiniteness. One with the Supreme Self.
Why do I want to be one with the supreme self? Because the limited self is not giving me joy and happiness. Therefore I want to transcend it. Its not that Im doing a favor to the Supreme.
Im joining his party. This state is not giving me joy and happiness which Im looking for. So I want to achieve a state which can give me joy and happiness.
And at that state, by all accounts we have seen is the only one state, the state of the Supreme Being. So everyone is knowingly or unknowingly trying to achieve that. We are failing and then going in circles.
The Bhagavan says, let me tell you, its a very simple and clear path. Act according to your nature. Do not do anything which is contrary to your nature.
Because that will complicate your life, will create more unnecessary vasanas, unnecessary desires and then unnecessary actions.

Verse 49 describes the ultimate state: asakta-buddhi (unattached intellect), jitatma (conquered self), vigata-spriha (free from longing) - such a person attains through sannyasa the supreme perfection of naishkarmya-siddhi, the state of actionlessness. This does not mean inactivity but rather action that leaves no karmic residue. When actions flow naturally from ones dharma without ego-driven attachment, they become like a hobby - full of engagement but without the burden of I am doing this for that result.
Verses 50-51 begin describing the path to Brahman. The process starts with buddhya vishuddhaya yukto - endowed with purified intellect, controlling the self with dhriti (steadfastness), abandoning sense objects, and casting aside raga-dvesha (attachment and aversion). This is the practical instruction: purify the intellect, establish control, renounce sensory preoccupation, and release the grip of likes and dislikes.
Today, examine your attachments and aversions: What are you currently pursuing (raga)? What are you currently avoiding (dvesha)? These twin forces keep us bound to the wheel of karma. The instruction is not to become indifferent but to vyudasya - cast aside the compulsive quality of attachment and aversion. You can still have preferences without being driven by them. Practice with one attachment today: notice it, acknowledge it, but do not act from its compulsion. Notice one aversion: face it rather than automatically avoiding it. This is the beginning of jitatma - conquering the self.
